newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says Americans should break race barriers.
newsitem.headline: Clinton says Americans should break race barriers.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Saturday outlined his vision for breaking down racial barriers, saying that creating a truly multi-racial democracy is the "unfinished work of our times."

"We have torn down the barriers in our laws. Now we must break down the barriers in our lives, our minds and our hearts," Clinton said in excerpts of a speech prepared for delivery at the University of California-San Diego commencement ceremonies.

Clinton said California's decision to repeal affirmative action programs granting preferences to minorities has been "dramatic and devastating" with minority enrollments in law school and other graduate programs plummeting for the first time in decades.

"Some of the brightest students won't even apply, they feel so unwelcome. Soon the same will likely happen in college. Call it what you will -- but I call it re-segregation. I have seen the damage segregation brought to my native South. America cannot make that mistake again," he said.

Clinton said that more than 30 years after the high tide of the civil rights movement, when America was judged to be divided into two countries, one black and one white, separate and unequal, that Americans face a choice.

"Will we become not two, but many Americas, separate, unequal and isolated? Or will we draw strength from all our people and our ancient faith in equality and human dignity to become the world's first truly multi-racial democracy? That is the unfinished work of our times: to lift the burden of race and redeem the promise of America," he said.
